utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't hear your question because there was a lot of interference in my headset. Could you repeat your question, please, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will repeat my question. You said that your father died on the 18th of August and that you buried him on the 19th. Did Mr. Zoran Zigic attend the funeral on the 19th of August?

utterances.speaker: MILE IVANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Zoran wasn't there, but his parents were there. His mother Savka and his father Nikola. They were there throughout that day. And I was with Zoran on the 18th. When Zoran expressed his condolences, that was on the 18th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the members from the Sikic family attend the funeral on the 19th?

utterances.speaker: MILE IVANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. His wife Soka and Sikic Ivica's mother, she was there too. The mother's name was Jela.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ivankovic, you said that Mr. Zoran Zigic was a very helpful person, a sociable person. Did you check as to why he did not attend your father's funeral on the 19th?

utterances.speaker: MILE IVANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, no, I didn't. He probably -- he was probably engaged elsewhere, but he paid tribute to my father because a family member was there and, actually, there were two of his family members who attended and he was -- had to do something elsewhere. He was probably taken up with some other business and couldn't come, was prevented from attending, but everybody else was there and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ivankovic, you said that Mr. Zoran Zigic was a sociable person. Have you seen him drunk or after taking liquor or alcohol?

utterances.speaker: MILE IVANKOVIC
utterances.text: When he was sober, he was an exceptionally good man, but when he drank, something happened to him. Something seemed to snap when he drank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain his behaviour when you said something snapped or something happened to him; was he aggressive?

utterances.speaker: MILE IVANKOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't that he was aggressive. I don't know what happens to a man when he drinks. I am not an alcoholic myself. I don't drink so I don't know actually know what happens in somebody's mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ivankovic, have you seen Mr. Zoran Zigic beat anybody?

utterances.speaker: MILE IVANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him beat anybody. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question: Have you heard that Mr. Zoran Zigic has beaten anybody?

utterances.speaker: MILE IVANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No. I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you. That concludes my cross-examination. Thank you Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Waidyaratne. Mr. Deretic, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence has no additional questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Thank you. Judge Fouad Riad has the floor. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Ivankovic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MILE IVANKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I just would like to understand something about your engagement in the Army of the Republika Srpska. You were mobilised. Was it -- were you a volunteer or were you mobilised like any other Serb, I mean as a duty?

utterances.speaker: MILE IVANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was -- on the 16th of September, I was mobilised. I got my call-up papers and responded, and it was a mixed unit with all ethnicities up until the 27th of June, 1992, and then I stayed on in the unit. It became another name -- another one, it turned into another unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And were there many other Croats with you or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MILE IVANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were Muslims, there were Croats in the unit too, on the 27th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And those who did not join or refused to get mobilised, what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: MILE IVANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, nothing happened to them. They just refused to be mobilised, although it was said that they would have to come up before a military court, but actually nothing happened to them, no action was taken. But most people responded. It was in 1991 when I responded to the call-up too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, you don't recall any incident concerning Mr. Zigic drinking, do you? You just mentioned something, he said something snapped. Could you just explain a little bit what happened, since you know him well?

utterances.speaker: MILE IVANKOVIC
utterances.text: Usually he was troubled by the injustices. He didn't like to see injustices when he would drink, but when he was sober, everything was normal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And what would he do to repair the injustice?

utterances.speaker: MILE IVANKOVIC
utterances.text: That was his nature, he was that kind of man. He would run in with his head where angels would fear to tread, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I mean, would he use violence?

utterances.speaker: MILE IVANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. He wasn't violent. Only if somebody did something to somebody else, he would come in and stand up for the person that was suffering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Fouad Riad. Mr. Ivankovic, we have no further questions to ask you. We thank you for being with us and we wish you every success in your work to come. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILE IVANKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you too, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers, I think that we still have some time left. Would you like to take up any matters, the ones you raised earlier on with respect to the documents perhaps? We can go on working up to 3.00 p.m. so take advantage of the time we have left, if you're ready to do so, of course. If not, we can go into that tomorrow. Tomorrow we only have one -- no. We have two witnesses for tomorrow so would you like to do it now or tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If I may take up your generous offer to use the time, Mr. Saxon has had the revised translation of this morning's exhibit Prosecution's 3/253, and if the registrar would be kind enough to distribute it, it was the one that was admitted but subject to revision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, would you like to assign a number to that document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I believe that was the number that was there.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number was 3/253. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: From last week's sessions, Your Honour, during the evidence of Witness DD/5, the Prosecution had identified and wished to have admitted into evidence a particular warrant. I will not give any details because it was done in private session, but it was Prosecution's Exhibit 3/252. It in fact was a warrant with a translation. And additionally, I believe my colleague Mr. Deretic had some photographs of Keraterm that were identified that were not moved into evidence, and again because we moved swiftly on from one witness to the next. So that was an outstanding matter and I don't know if the Chamber would also wish to consider these two items together as they came during the testimony of Witness DD/5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I am going to give the floor to Mr. Deretic to hear his position, and I'll ask him afterwards whether he does want to or not admit into evidence the documents that we -- the photographs we used. Mr. Deretic, let's hear your response.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, at all events, we will tender the photographs. We were going to do that on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me for interrupting. The first question, objection or not, with respect to the documents put forward by the Prosecutor? That is to say 3/253 -- 2. I said 2. I said 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are opposed because procedure is underway by which we hope to receive a written document from the CBS Prijedor, and according to that document, a wanted warrant was never issued for Witness DD/5, and that is what we claimed here. That is precisely what we were saying, what we claimed. And in that sense and along those lines, we consider that it would be best and useful if the Chamber allow the Defence to state its views in the course of the coming week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That means that you would like to consider the tendering into evidence of these documents next week when you have additional information, additional documents; is that right? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I believe that is entirely out of order, Your Honour. If the other side wishes to contest a matter raised, there is the rebuttal case and that is the appropriate time. This document's relevance, I think, was very clear. In fact, it was addressed by the witness during cross-examination. The facts contained in the document were acknowledged by the witness. Its relevance is unquestionable. If counsel wishes to discuss something about it, the appropriate time would be rebuttal, not now. He is finished with his witness during his case in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what my learned colleague of the Prosecution is saying is so, that's quite right, but the Defence has been objecting throughout, and in our legal system, from the time an order is issued until a wanted warrant is issued, it is an unwieldy, long procedure, which we call an administrative procedure, and we say -- we claim that a wanted warrant was never issued for that particular witness, and we are going to substantiate that by using documents. We shall prove it with documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we ought to end this discussion. Ms. Susan Somers, would you like to add anything quickly?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I only repeat that that is a ground for rebuttal. It has nothing to do with the issue at hand. It would be appropriate to admit it. If there is some refutation later, so be it, but at this time it's a valid document, in our view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The judges will confer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber admits the document, Exhibit 3/252, and at the opportune moment, we'll see what probative value it has and what weight it will attach. The Defence has the right to prove otherwise. For the moment, in line with our Rules, that is our ruling. Ms. Susan Somers, anything else for the moment? I think this brings us to the photographs and Mr. Deretic. Mr. Deretic, you used a set of photographs. Would you like to have them admitted into evidence or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you remind us of the photographs in question, which were they?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D10/4, D11/4, D12/4, D13/4, D14/4, D15/4, D16/4, D17/4, D18/4 -- I'm sorry, up until D17/4. D17/4 is the last photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm looking at the original numbering that was on the album that I have. It does vary a little bit. If the Chamber does admit, I would ask that it do so with a caveat that some of these photos demonstrate on the reverse side that they are taken very recently, and do not portray Keraterm as it was during the time relevant to the indictment. Therefore, there will be some points of variance in physical appearance and also internal, if any are internal photos. The numbering that I have reflects a K numbering and I think that it was -- it's been redone -- okay. It's been redone completely. I'm sorry. Again, if the Chamber -- we would have no objection, only asking the Chamber that it take note of the dates on them and that -- in its review or any weight that it attaches to the photos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No translation].

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Sorry, Judge Rodrigues, I didn't catch that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Susan Somers, we took note of that. I, too, suddenly saw that they were photographs not taken at the time of the offence, but more recent photographs, as you say. And we have -- the album was distributed. It contains photographs of Keraterm and Omarska but we used just several of them and it is those that are going to be admitted into evidence, so not all of them, just the photographs that were utilised; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: That was my understanding. That's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there was one item, unfortunately I don't have it with me today, I wasn't aware we'd have these few moments, but it was Prosecution's Exhibit 3/249 which required a review, as it were, by the translation section. I have received the document back and I will bring it to the session tomorrow with the comments by the translation section. It was a document signed -- reporting to be signed by Sikirica. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please, the Judges will confer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibits -- defence exhibits D10 to D17 inclusive, all of them /4, are all admitted into evidence. Mr. Deretic, I think that for tomorrow, we only have one witness; is that right? Am I correct in understanding that, and that will be [redacted] is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. However, we do have one more witness but it is a witness for the Prcac Defence. So in fact we have two witnesses, one of them belonging to the Zigic Defence case and the second one belonging to the Prcac Defence case. I have already consulted my colleague from the Prcac Defence team, and I think that we will need up to the lunch break. That is to say, up to 1.00, that that will be sufficient for us to complete our examination of the first witness -- of that witness, and I assume that the Prcac Defence in the time after lunch will have enough time to get through their witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Deretic. I was just asking about the Zigic witness, but just to confer, Mr. Jovan Simic you have the floor. Would you like to bring us up to date about your witnesses? Mr. Deretic, you are not in charge of the Prcac Defence case. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, tomorrow, we envisage our own witness, Mr. Drasko Dzervida, is to testify tomorrow, according to your decision, after the witness for the Zigic Defence case. I should just like to make a proposal, if I may with your indulgence. We discussed this with Ms. Somers, and she considers, and that is the position of the Zigic Defence team, that they will need quite a bit of time for the examination of their witness. And I should like to propose as food for thought, and if the Prosecution agrees, that we perhaps hear our witness first, that is to say, Mr. Dzervida first. Because if we run into a situation whereby we don't succeed in getting through the other witness before the end of business in view of his family situation and everything else, it would be very difficult if he had to stay on for another day. So technically, perhaps we could reverse the witnesses. We would not need too much time, just half an hour for the examination-in-chief for our witness. It would take shorter for our witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you say "here," you mean "there," in Banja Luka, not actually here in The Hague, there in Banja Luka. Is that what you actually mean? MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, Mr. Deretic. Do you agree with that procedure, with that proposal just made?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We agree absolutely, Mr. President, because it is also in our interest to complete the videolinks, and I think that the proposal is a justified and valid one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Very well. We shall try and get through both witnesses tomorrow. Ms. Susan Somers, do you have an observation to make?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: This is the first time we've discussed reversing the order, but I think -- I wonder if the Chamber would possibly inquire the total amount of time that the Defence for Zigic anticipates for [redacted], if there's a realistic estimate at this point in time, if it might be possible to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers, the information that I received is one hour, but I think that was the anticipated time at the beginning. But -- that it might drop to half an hour. Mr. Deretic, you're here, so you can give us an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, perhaps I didn't understand you and my learned colleague correctly, but our examination will certainly last between one and a half to two hours. I think that we shall be over by 3.00. So for us, four hours, and the Prcac Defence an additional hour, which means that we would end by the end of tomorrow's working day, counting everything altogether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How much time do you need for the Prcac witness, Mr. Simic? Give us an estimate. How much time do you need for your witness? You might have said but could you repeat? MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] About 30 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers, any further information that you need?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In which case, if the Chamber is minded to reverse the order, I think it would be helpful to have the Prcac witness go first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you agree, is that it? You agree to have the order reversed? Very well. Then we shall begin the day tomorrow with the witness for the Prcac Defence, and then we will go on to hear the witness for the Zigic Defence case. I think that's all for today. We reconvene tomorrow morning at 9.20, as usual. A pleasant afternoon's work and we reconvene tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
